examples.text: Auf dem Hügel stand eine Trauerweide.
„Ich wünschte, die Trauerweide wäre nie richtig angegangen, wäre eingegangen, verkümmert.“
„Hinter den Fenstern, an denen das Wasser in Strömen herabrann, stand eine Trauerweide mit ausgehöhltem Stamm, deren haarfeine Äste in alle Richtungen gepeitscht wurden.“
„Ich blickte auf die mit dreckigem Schnee bedeckte deutsche Erde in unserem Garten, zum Rhein, über die Trauerweiden hinweg aufs Siebengebirge, und diese ganze Szenerie kam mir idiotisch vor.“
„Die Trauerweiden waren umgestürzt; die Wurzeln schienen dadurch die Äste zu sein, und die Zweige lange, schleifende grüne Wurzeln.“

examples.text: A notorious human crybaby, according to her older siblings, parents and the building superintendent, will cry for two hours every two hours, refusing to acknowledge any distinction between crying and other basic infant activities, like “being awake” or “breathing.”

glosses: Someone whose feelings are very easily hurt, often by trivial matters.

examples.text: Then he used the occasion to humiliate the provost, calling her an example of the censorious crybabies whom he had come to relieve of their responsibility.

glosses: Someone who takes offense or excessively complains when things are not going well.

examples.text: […]Now there are a lot of crybabies around who are talking about what ought to have done and the bomb ought to have had a demonstration in Japan before you killed all those people. […] I don't care what the crybabies say now because they didn't have to make the decision.

glosses: To act like a crybaby.

examples.text: Out: Trash talk, dirty play, crybabying, showboating and players who can't be bothered to show up for games or keep their shoes on.
